item.title: Generation of discrete breathers from linear to nonlinear Anderson disorder in electrical lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.38116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate linear and nonlinear localization in a disordered electrical lattice composed of coupled LC resonators. In the linear regime, the normal-mode spectrum and spatial voltage profiles are characterized theoretically and experimentally, revealing strongly localized Anderson modes induced by capacitive disorder. Good agreement is found between numerical predictions and experimental measurements of resonance frequencies, spatial profiles, inverse participation ratios, and localization lengths. Nonlinearity is introduced through varactor diodes, allowing the numerical continuation of a selected Anderson-localized mode into a family of discrete breathers. Floquet analysis indicates that these nonlinear localized solutions remain spectrally stable over the investigated frequency range, while their spatial localization evolves with increasing amplitude. Experimental measurements reveal nonlinear resonance bending, frequency shifts, and hysteresis, in qualitative agreement with the predicted nonlinear behavior. These results provide numerical evidence for the emergence of stable, disorder-pinned discrete breathers from Anderson-localized modes, supported by experimental observations of the associated nonlinear resonant response, and highlight the interplay between disorder and nonlinearity in electrical lattices.
item.dc:creator: Xuan-Lin Chen, F. Palmero

item.title: Series approximation of discrete-soliton solutions of the DNLS equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study standing waves of the discrete nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger (DNLS) equation by means of perturbative series expansions in the inter-site coupling parameter $\varepsilon$. Power-series approximations are derived for three representative configurations: a single-site soliton and the two two-site ones, namely the in-phase and the out-of-phase configurations. Although higher-order truncations are increasingly accurate for small $\varepsilon$, the expansions possess a small radius of convergence and cease to be useful well before $\varepsilon={\cal O}(1)$. To extend their range of validity we apply the Euler convergence-acceleration method, constructing an optimally transformed series for each lattice site individually. The transformed solution is shown to have substantially better convergence radius and preserves the localization of the solution much better than the original series solution. We then insert the series profiles into the linearization matrix of the DNLS equation in order to obtain improved approximations of the stability eigenvalues, with particular attention to the unstable real eigenvalue of the in-phase configuration. Optimal truncation of the corresponding expansion yields a closed-form ${\cal O}(\varepsilon^{5/2})$ estimate, which significantly extends the known ${\cal O}(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ leading-order result to considerably larger couplings, while the semi-numerical use of the accelerated profiles reproduces the numerically computed eigenvalue to values of $\varepsilon$ of ${\cal O}(1)$. Throughout, both the solution profiles and their stability eigenvalues are benchmarked against the numerical solution obtained through a continuation procedure from the anti-continuum limit.
item.dc:creator: V. Tsiantou, V. Koukouloyannis, K. D. Housiadas, P. G. Kevrekidis

item.title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.40103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Alice C. Quillen, Laura Quinonez

item.title: Symmetry-resolved periods in a cyclic-dominance automaton: separating intrinsic from lattice-induced periodicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.37990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodic attractors of spatially extended systems possess not one period but a hierarchy of periods, one for each level of observation and symmetry quotient, and this hierarchy separates how a pattern evolves from how it fits the finite domain. For a synchronous threshold model of cyclic dominance on an $L\times L$ torus, equivalent to the three-color cyclic cellular automaton of Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath, we measure for every attractor a \emph{tuple} of periods: that of the populations ($\Tpop$), of the full configuration ($\Tst$), and of the configuration up to color rotations ($\Tcol$), lattice symmetries ($\Tgeo$) and the full space--color group ($\TG$). Equivariance implies exact divisibility relations and the factorization $\Tst=\TG\,m$, where $m$ counts the applications of the symmetry $h$ that maps the configuration onto itself after $\TG$ steps: $\TG$ and the type of $h$ belong to the pattern, $m$ to the lattice, and the attractors are relative periodic orbits whose full period emerges from the interaction between the intrinsic dynamics and the lattice symmetries. A family of attractors built around a pair of counter-rotating spirals, with $\Tpop=24$ and $\TG=8$, persists from $L=9$ to $L=40$ while $\Tst$ takes values from 24 to 960, given in every case by the order of $h$; on a rectangular $9\times12$ torus it takes the value 48, absent from all square tori. With more than $4.5\times10^5$ runs at each of $L=8$ and $L=9$ we estimate the basins of attraction: fixed points take 95--97\% of the configuration space, and no single period is enough to tell the oscillating attractors apart. The same analysis locates local diversity: it is balanced whenever the cycle has a color symmetry and, on large lattices, it is concentrated at the spiral cores.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no

item.title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. We test the method on a stochastic pitchfork model and a spatial stochastic Swift-Hohenberg equation. In both models, classification improves with longer observation horizons, closer proximity to the bifurcation, stronger noise, and larger nonlinear effects. However, these conditions are also linked to a higher risk of noise-induced tipping in the subcritical case. The useful early-warning window is therefore determined by a balance between obtaining enough information to identify the bifurcation type and doing so before noise-induced tipping becomes too likely. In spatially extended systems, we find that observing the full spatial field allows classification over shorter observation horizons, and performance improves when a broader range of spatial modes contributes to the observed dynamics. Altogether, we identify the conditions under which the method can reliably distinguish between supercritical and subcritical bifurcations.
item.dc:creator: Paul A. Sanders, Christian Kuehn, Bastian Hilder, Robbin Bastiaansen

item.title: Existence and spectral instability of steady rolls in the Nikolaevskiy equation: a computer-assisted study
item.description: arXiv:2610.39611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Nikolaevskiy equation is a model of short-wave pattern formation coupled to a neutral long-wave mode, and it is believed that all of its spatially periodic steady states are unstable. Existing results are formal, numerical, or restricted to a small neighbourhood of onset. We give computer-assisted proofs of three results. First, for every wavenumber q in [0.9, 1.1] and every control parameter r between the onset value (1-q^2)^2 and 4, the equation has a nontrivial, real-analytic, odd steady roll; these rolls form a single continuous two-parameter family that bifurcates from the trivial state at onset, with an explicit amplitude bound proportional to the square root of the distance to onset. Second, every roll of this family with r in [0.25, 4] is spectrally unstable on the real line: its linearisation has a Bloch eigenvalue with real part at least 6.7e-4, and at least 0.13 for r >= 0.575. Third, at nine sample points we enclose, at a small Bloch number, the eigenvalue numerically identified with the long-wave (Matthews-Cox) branch; its real part is positive at seven points and negative at two, while strongly unstable eigenvalues exist at all nine. The proofs combine a parametrised Newton-Kantorovich theorem, a desingularisation near onset, Taylor-model bounds on parameter boxes, and a Weyl-sequence argument for the Bloch spectrum; all estimates are evaluated in rigorous interval arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Nikita V. Konev, Fedor A. Vyazanitsyn, Igor A. Knyazev

item.title: Wave Turbulence of Capillary Waves in Finite Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.40217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider classical problem of turbulence of capillary waves. In a series of numerical simulations it is shown that Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum corresponding to direct cascade of energy has a limited dynamic range of realization in a finite system, which shrinks with decreasing level of nonlinearity. Recent hypothesis that this dynamic range scales with average steepness as $\sim\mu^{8/3}$ is confirmed. As a byproduct the Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum was observed for record dynamic range close to or beyond one decade in a variety of simulation configurations.
item.dc:creator: Alexander O. Korotkevich
